title: Interleaved Fetch Proxy & Stable Prefetch Hinting for Pagination API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The Console dashboard query API serves a broad range of paginated explorations for tenants with widely varying temporal windows and card sizes. Recent telemetry shows p95 tail latency spikes driven by cold KV cache lookups when users page rapidly across partitions and by bursty fanout reads for multi-entity cards. Existing prefetch heuristics are coarse and often materialize unnecessary prefixes, increasing IO and increasing read amplification for large tenants.

Goal: Implement an Interleaved Fetch Proxy layer that stitches async prefetches with on-demand reads and exposes stable prefetch hint signals to the dashboard pagination coordinator. The proxy should: (1) allow low-latency point requests to observe in-flight prefetches and join them, (2) emit compact prefetch hint summaries (per-tenant, per-card) to the pagination controller so it can make lookahead decisions, and (3) respect cross-tenant isolation and rate limits.

Design overview:
- Interleaved Fetch Proxy (IFP): a lightweight service sitting between the query planner and the KV read layer. It maintains short-lived in-memory inflight fetch index entries and a small LRU for hot prefix fragments. Requests hitting an inflight fetch join the existing future; requests for adjacent ranges receive a best-effort streamed partial response while a background consolidation read completes.
- Prefetch hinting API: IFP generates time-windowed hint summaries (bitmap + estimated cardinality + confidence) at configurable TTLs. The pagination coordinator subscribes to these hints via a bounded async publish path and uses them to adapt lookahead depth and batch size. Hints are tenant-scoped and scrubbed of PII.
- Backpressure and throttling: IFP enforces per-tenant concurrency quotas and a token-bucket on background prefetches. When capacity is limited, the coordination policy favors low-latency foreground reads and postpones prefetches for low-confidence hints.
- Consistency model: Strong consistency for single-page reads is preserved; prefetches are treated as opportunistic read-through caches with conservative staleness window (configurable, default 5s).

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs. latency: keeping larger inflight indexes reduces duplicate reads but increases memory. We limit in-memory index to ~256k entries and evict least-recently-used tenant prefixes to avoid noisy-tenant blowups.
- Hint fidelity vs. cost: emitting high-resolution histograms is costly. We use bitmap + cardinality estimate to balance utility and payload size.
- Push vs. pull hints: Push reduces decision latency but adds load; we implement a push with backpressure and fallback to on-demand fetch when subscription fails.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype IFP as an independent binary behind a feature flag with no hinting; basic inflight join + LRU fragment cache. Load-test single-tenant scenarios.
2) Add prefetch hinting format and bounded pub/sub to pagination coordinator. Integrate tenant-safe summaries.
3) Implement throttling policies and graceful degradation (when IFP disabled, dashboard falls back to current behavior).
4) End-to-end integration testing, stress tests with mixed-tenant workloads, and rollout via canary lanes in console-2025.11.

Telemetry and success metrics:
- Primary: reduce dashboard query p95 for paginated card reads by 20% under mixed workloads.
- Secondary: reduce duplicate KV read traffic by 30% for targeted tenants, and decrease per-token backend cost for small-page churn scenarios by 15%.
- Safety: no increase in error rate (5xx) and no breaches of per-tenant read quotas during canary.

Rollback strategy: Feature is gated by a console flag and a per-cluster IFP toggle. If p95 worsens or error rates increase, toggle off IFP and revert to the previous routing within 1 hour.

Notes on data privacy: Hints must not include raw keys or query payloads. We will apply deterministic hashing and aggregation at tenant granularity and run a quick privacy review to ensure no leakage in produced summaries.
acceptance_criteria: IFP prototype joins inflight reads and reduces duplicate KV invocations in bench harness
Pagination coordinator consumes prefetch hints and adapts lookahead depth with measurable latency improvement
End-to-end canary demonstrates >=20% p95 reduction for paginated card reads on mixed workloads
No increase in 5xx errors or quota violations during canary
Documentation for operators (runbooks) and a migration playbook for tenants exist
